1.OA.A.1: Add and subtract within 20 to solve word problems, using objects, drawings and equations.
1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that add three whole numbers with a sum of 20 or less.
1.OA.B.3: Use properties of operations (order, grouping) as strategies to add and subtract.
1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (count on 2 to add 2).
1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20 fluently within 10, using strategies such as making ten.
1.OA.D.7: Understand the equal sign and decide whether equations are true or false.
1.OA.D.8: Find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation.
1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120 from any number; read, write and represent numbers to 120.
1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number are tens and ones.
1.NBT.B.2a: Understand 10 as a bundle of ten ones, called a ten.
1.NBT.B.2b: Understand 11 to 19 as a ten and some ones.
1.NBT.B.2c: Understand 10, 20, …, 90 as some number of tens and 0 ones.
1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers using tens and ones, with >, = and <.
1.NBT.C.4: Add within 100 using models, place value and properties; sometimes make a ten.
1.NBT.C.5: Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number mentally.
1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 (within 10–90).
1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare two lengths using a third object.
1.MD.A.2: Measure length with whole numbers of same-size units laid end to end.
1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours.
1.MD.C.4: Organize, show and interpret data with up to three categories.
1.G.A.1: Tell defining attributes of shapes (sides, corners) from non-defining ones (color, size).
1.G.A.2: Put together two- and three-dimensional shapes to make new shapes.
1.G.A.3: Split circles and rectangles into two or four equal shares (halves, fourths).
2.OA.A.1: Add and subtract within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems.
2.OA.B.2: Add and subtract within 20 fluently; know all sums of two one-digit numbers.
2.OA.C.3: Decide whether a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even.
2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total in a rectangular array of up to 5 rows and 5 columns.
2.NBT.A.1: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number are hundreds, tens and ones.
2.NBT.A.1a: Understand 100 as a bundle of ten tens, called a hundred.
2.NBT.A.1b: Understand 100, 200, …, 900 as some number of hundreds and 0 tens and ones.
2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers with >, = and <.
2.NBT.B.5: Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value and properties.
2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.
2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within 1,000 using models, place value and properties.
2.NBT.B.8: Add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from a number between 100 and 900 mentally.
2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value.
2.MD.A.1: Measure length with rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks and measuring tapes.
2.MD.A.2: Measure an object twice with different units and relate the two measurements.
2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
2.MD.A.4: Measure how much longer one object is than another.
2.MD.B.5: Add and subtract within 100 to solve word problems about lengths.
2.MD.B.6: Show whole numbers as lengths on a number line and add and subtract on it.
2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems with dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.
2.MD.D.9: Measure lengths and show the measurements on a line plot.
2.MD.D.10: Draw picture graphs and bar graphs and solve problems with their data.
2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes with given attributes (triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, cubes).
2.G.A.2: Split a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count them.
2.G.A.3: Split circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal shares.
3.OA.A.1: Understand multiplication as equal groups (5 × 7 is 5 groups of 7).
3.OA.A.2: Understand division as sharing equally or making equal groups.
3.OA.A.3: Multiply and divide within 100 to solve word problems with equal groups, arrays and measures.
3.OA.A.4: Find the unknown number in a multiplication or division equation.
3.OA.B.5: Use the properties of multiplication (order, grouping, distributing) as strategies.
3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
3.OA.C.7: Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know all products of two one-digit numbers.
3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems with the four operations; check if answers are reasonable.
3.OA.D.9: Find and explain patterns in arithmetic, such as in the multiplication table.
3.NBT.A.1: Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
3.NBT.A.2: Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently using place value and properties.
3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 (9 × 80).
3.NF.A.1: Understand a unit fraction 1/b as one of b equal parts, and a/b as a of those parts.
3.NF.A.2a: Show 1/b on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into b equal parts.
3.NF.A.2b: Show a/b on a number line as a lengths of 1/b from 0.
3.NF.A.3a: Understand two fractions as equivalent when they are the same size or point.
3.NF.A.3b: Recognize and make simple equivalent fractions and explain why they are equal.
3.NF.A.3c: Write whole numbers as fractions and recognize fractions equal to whole numbers.
3.NF.A.3d: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator.
3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and solve problems about elapsed time.
3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in liters, grams and kilograms.
3.MD.B.3: Draw scaled picture graphs and bar graphs and solve problems with them.
3.MD.B.4: Measure lengths to the nearest half and fourth inch and show them on a line plot.
3.MD.C.5a: Understand a unit square as having an area of one square unit.
3.MD.C.5b: Understand that a shape covered by n unit squares has an area of n square units.
3.MD.C.6: Measure area by counting unit squares.
3.MD.C.7a: Find the area of a rectangle by tiling it and show it equals length times width.
3.MD.C.7b: Multiply side lengths to find the area of rectangles in real-world problems.
3.MD.C.7c: Use tiling to show the distributive property with areas.
3.MD.C.7d: Find the area of figures made of rectangles by adding the areas of the parts.
3.MD.D.8: Solve problems about perimeters of polygons, including an unknown side length.
3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories can share attributes; classify quadrilaterals.
3.G.A.2: Split shapes into parts with equal areas and write each part as a unit fraction.
4.OA.A.1: Read a multiplication equation as a comparison (35 is 5 times as many as 7).
4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems about multiplicative comparison.
4.OA.A.3: Solve multi-step word problems with whole numbers, including remainders.
4.OA.C.5: Make and analyze a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule.
4.NBT.A.1: Understand that a digit is ten times what it would be one place to the right.
4.NBT.A.2: Read, write and compare multi-digit whole numbers in several forms.
4.NBT.A.3: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
4.NBT.B.4: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
4.NBT.B.5: Multiply up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number, and two two-digit numbers.
4.NBT.B.6: Divide up to four-digit dividends by one-digit divisors, with remainders.
4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and denominators.
4.NF.B.3a: Understand adding and subtracting fractions as joining and separating parts of the same whole.
4.NF.B.3b: Break a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way.
4.NF.B.3c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
4.NF.B.3d: Solve word problems adding and subtracting fractions with like denominators.
4.NF.B.4a: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
4.NF.B.4b: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and multiply a fraction by a whole number.
4.NF.B.4c: Solve word problems multiplying a fraction by a whole number.
4.NF.C.5: Write a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 and add them.
4.NF.C.6: Write fractions with denominator 10 or 100 as decimals.
4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units and convert from larger to smaller units.
4.MD.A.2: Solve word problems about distance, time, volume, mass and money with the four operations.
4.MD.A.3: Use the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world problems.
4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot of measurements in fractions of a unit and solve problems with it.
4.MD.C.5a: Understand an angle as turning through a fraction of a circle; a one-degree angle is 1/360 of a turn.
4.MD.C.5b: Understand that an angle turning through n one-degree angles measures n degrees.
4.MD.C.6: Measure and draw angles in whole-number degrees with a protractor.
4.MD.C.7: Add angle measures and find an unknown angle in a diagram.
4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures by parallel and perpendicular lines and by angle size.
5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions for calculations and read expressions without evaluating them.
5.NBT.B.5: Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
5.NBT.B.6: Divide up to four-digit dividends by two-digit divisors.
5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths.
5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators.
5.NF.B.3: Understand a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator.
5.NF.B.4a: Understand (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts.
5.NF.B.4b: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling.
5.NF.B.5a: Compare the size of a product to the size of one factor without multiplying.
5.NF.B.5b: Explain why multiplying by a fraction greater or less than 1 makes a product greater or smaller.
5.NF.B.6: Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
5.NF.B.7a: Divide a unit fraction by a whole number.
5.NF.B.7b: Divide a whole number by a unit fraction.
5.NF.B.7c: Solve real-world problems dividing unit fractions and whole numbers.
5.MD.B.2: Make a line plot of measurements in fractions of a unit and solve problems with it.
5.MD.C.3a: Understand a unit cube as having a volume of one cubic unit.
5.MD.C.3b: Understand that a solid packed with n unit cubes has a volume of n cubic units.
5.MD.C.4: Measure volume by counting unit cubes.
5.MD.C.5a: Find the volume of a rectangular prism by packing it and show it equals length × width × height.
5.MD.C.5b: Use V = l × w × h and V = B × h to find volumes of rectangular prisms.
5.MD.C.5c: Find volumes of solids made of two rectangular prisms by adding their volumes.
5.G.A.1: Understand the coordinate plane: axes, origin, and ordered pairs.
5.G.A.2: Graph points in the first quadrant to solve real-world problems.
5.G.B.4: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy by their properties.
